input:
<question>
How do I get access to the export-controlled drawings folder for my program?
</question>
<passages>
[KB-104 §1] Request access to a CAD vault project folder - Request access to a CAD vault project folder
Project folders are restricted by program. Request access through the IT service portal: **Request > Engineering applications > CAD vault folder access**. Your manager approves standard folders within one business day.

Export-controlled folders are not covered by this article and are not granted through this request.

[KB-602 §1] Share a drawing with a supplier - Share a drawing with a supplier
Drawings go to suppliers only through the supplier portal, never by email. Choose **Share > Supplier portal**, pick the supplier, and the portal records when they acknowledge it. Export-controlled drawings need a Trade Compliance check before sharing; the portal blocks them until it is done.

[KB-702 §1] CAD client crashes when opening large drawings - CAD client crashes when opening large drawings
Set **Options > Performance > Large assembly mode** on, and turn off **Shaded previews** for drawings. If it still crashes, the graphics driver may be outdated: install the version listed on the engineering workstation page.

[KB-502 §1] Sign in to the PLM with single sign-on - Sign in to the PLM with single sign-on
The PLM uses company single sign-on. If you see **Access denied** after signing in, your PLM role has not been granted yet (see KB-501). If the sign-in page loops, clear your browser cookies for the PLM site and try again in a private window.

[KB-701 §1] Fix 'missing references' when opening an assembly - Fix 'missing references' when opening an assembly
Missing references usually mean parts were renamed or moved outside the vault. Open the assembly from the vault (not from a local folder), choose **Tools > Resolve references > From vault**, and check in the assembly after it opens cleanly.

[KB-102 §1] Check in a large assembly without timeouts - Check in a large assembly without timeouts
Check-ins of assemblies with more than 2,000 components can time out over VPN.

1. Close every drawing that references the assembly.
2. In the vault client choose **Check in > Selected files only** and check in the changed parts first, then the top assembly.
3. If you are on VPN, use the **Remote Site cache**: set **Tools > Options > Site** to your nearest site before checking in.

If a check-in still fails, the client log is in **Help > Show log folder**; attach `vault-client.log` to a ticket.
</passages>

steps.text: The standard CAD vault folder access request does not cover export-controlled folders, so access to them is not granted through that request.

cites.quote: Export-controlled folders are not covered by this article and are not granted through this request.

output.ticket_summary: Engineer needs access to their program's export-controlled drawings folder; the knowledge base does not describe how this access is requested or granted.
